name: ch4_rate_burst_stress
description: Finite-correlation rate-burst stress test for the measured-error autonomous scrub policy.
purpose: Check whether the autonomous measured-error policy remains admissible when the hourly Chapter 3 rate series is modulated by finite-duration sub-hourly rate bursts.
The model preserves the hourly mean rate from data/ch3_five_year_upsets.csv and changes only the temporal concentration of the rate within each hour.

This is the primary burst-stress model because finite-correlation rate bursts are period-sensitive: shorter scrub periods can resolve the burst, unlike the pass-level constant-VMR negative-binomial counterexample.

baselines.name: always_tau_min_1s
baselines.role: conservative lower-period reference within the accumulated-risk model

rate_burst_model.hourly_mean_preservation: normalize multipliers inside each hour so the time average of g(t) over the hour is exactly 1
notes: rate_cv2=0 is the Poisson sanity case and is independent of burst_duration_seconds.
burst_duration_seconds controls the finite correlation time of the rate multiplier.
This model stresses temporally resolved accumulated single-error arrivals, not instantaneous MBU/MCU mapping.

simulation.risk_convention: pathwise additive risk E_path = sum_i -log(1 - p_acc_given_k(K_i)); P_path = 1 - exp(-E_path)
simulation.history_edge_rule: At the beginning of the mission the policy starts from initial_index; no unavailable prior history is required.
simulation.observability_assumption: The policy observes the realized corrected-error count K_i for the completed pass. This is the same idealized observation convention as the existing measured-policy simulations.

pre_registered_prediction: The rate_cv2=0 sanity case should reproduce the existing Poisson measured-policy seed-sweep within Monte Carlo tolerance.
The final focused grid is selected from the pilot run before increasing seed_count from 5 to 30.
The admissible boundary is expected between rate_cv2=0.5 and 0.75 for 300 s and 600 s bursts, between 0.75 and 1.0 for 900 s bursts, and above 1.0 for 1800 s bursts.
The boundary is expected to move to lower admissible rate_cv2 as burst_duration_seconds decreases.
The always_tau_min_1s baseline is expected to remain sampled-admissible on the tested finite-correlation grid, but no claim is made for arbitrary unbounded burstiness.
Failures are interpreted as the boundary between temporally resolvable accumulated single-error control and unresolved burst/instantaneous mechanisms.
